title: Which ZDX API operations the Python and Go SDKs cover, and the configuration API neither calls
aliases: can i create a zdx probe via api

prose.text: Each SDK's ZDX functions and the contract's operations are generated side by side by `node scripts/kb.mjs surface zdx`. This subject records the coverage differences that change what a caller can automate.

prose.label: Configuration.
prose.text: The application management operations are in [[zdx.applications:config-api]]. {{config-family}} No SDK calls any of them: [[zdx.applications:config-no-sdk]].

prose.label: Writes the SDKs do cover.
prose.text: Starting and deleting deep traces: [[zdx.diagnostics.start-request]] and [[zdx.diagnostics.session-records]]. Score analysis: [[zdx.diagnostics.analysis]]. Alert snapshots: [[zdx.alerts.snapshot]].

checks.do: Whether the task needs the `/v1/config` operations (applications, monitors, collections, tracing), which have to be called directly because no SDK wraps them.
Whether a Go integration needs deep-trace metrics, app users or snapshots, which only the Python SDK wraps.

config-family.statement: Besides application management, the contract's `/v1/config` family writes monitors, collections and tracing sessions (updating monitors, creating collections, creating and starting tracing sessions) and reads users, devices, departments, groups and locations as configuration.

Config User Resource List Config Users
Config Device Resource List Config Devices

snapshots-python-alert-only.statement: Only the Python SDK wraps a snapshot operation, the alert snapshot; no Go package covers snapshots, and neither SDK calls the contract's user snapshot.
snapshots-python-alert-only.conditions: Rests on the generated surface: the Go SDK's ZDX packages are administration, alerts, common, inventory, reports and troubleshooting, and no SDK endpoint matches `/snapshot/user`.

go-deeptrace-functions.statement: The Go `deeptrace` package has four functions, `GetDeepTraces`, `GetDeepTraceSession`, `CreateDeepTraceSession` and `DeleteDeepTraceSession`; the deep trace's top processes are read by `GetDeviceTopProcesses` in the `reports/devices` package.

go-deeptrace-functions.conditions: The four quoted functions are every function `deeptrace.go` defines at the pin.

python-deeptrace-readers.statement: So the deep trace's web-probe metrics, cloud-path metrics, cloud path, health metrics and events are readable through the Python SDK (`get_deeptrace_webprobe_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_cloudpath_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_cloudpath`, `get_deeptrace_health_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_events`) but have no Go function; the Go device report functions read the device's own paths, not a trace's.

python-deeptrace-readers.conditions: Rests on the generated surface: no Go endpoint matches a `/deeptraces/` metric path other than top processes.

app-users-python-only.statement: Listing an application's users and reading one user's experience with it (`list_app_users`, `get_app_user`) are Python-only; the Go `reports/applications` package has `GetAllApps`, `GetApp`, `GetAppScores` and `GetAppMetrics`.

app-users-python-only.conditions: Rests on the generated surface: the Go package's functions map to no `/apps/{id}/users` path.

go-device-filters.statement: The Go device list cannot filter by MAC address or private IPv4: its `GetDevicesFilters` carries user IDs, emails, location, department, geolocation, offset and limit beside the shared time filters, while the contract and the Python `list_devices` offer `mac_address` and `private_ipv4`.

quotes: ``[query_params.private_ipv4]`` {str}: Private IPv4 address of the device.

go-device-filters.conditions: The quoted fields are the whole `GetDevicesFilters` struct, and the embedded `GetFromToFilters` has no MAC or IPv4 field at the pin. How Python sends these names is in zdx.sdk-python.request-shaping.
